title: Team Leaders Should Not Be the Only Ones With Coaching Assignments
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece addresses a structural problem in leader-as-coach models: a single leader cannot provide every team member the coaching attention they need. The proposed solution is distributing short, rotating coaching assignments among team members themselves, ranging from skill-sharing to peer feedback to joint problem-solving. The author notes a secondary benefit -- people who coach others become more receptive to coaching themselves -- and argues that peer coaching frees the team leader to focus their own limited coaching time where it has the greatest impact.
points: A single team leader cannot personally deliver all the coaching every team member needs.
Rotating, short-term peer coaching assignments spread that developmental load across the team.
Team members who coach others tend to become more receptive to coaching themselves.
Distributing coaching frees the leader to concentrate their own time where it matters most.
quotes: Everyone on the team needs the attention of the leader as coach.
Leveraging the entire team and asking each member to play a coaching role is how the best leaders solve this dilemma.
These are not permanent assignments. In fact, most last for only a handful of days or a couple of weeks.
It seems becoming the teacher changes the way a student learns.
The best leaders unlock the wisdom and skills of the collective team so they can unlock the potential of every team member.
